newsitem.title: USA: US money managers remain bullish on US debt - MCM.
newsitem.headline: US money managers remain bullish on US debt - MCM.

text.p: Fixed-income managers grew marginally more bullish in the face of a minor selloff of U.S. debt last week, according to the latest MCM MoneyWatch Inc asset allocation survey.

"Investors are maintaining bullish exposure without having to go all the way out the curve," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague. "Investors are reaching for yield, so (they) want to be invested."
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 106.1 percent in the week ended September 9 from 105.7 percent in the prior week.

A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market. A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 19 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," down from 20 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" dropped to 22 percent, down from 24 percent in the week ended September 3.
Fifty-nine percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 56 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets fell to 2.96 percent, against 3.10 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 24 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 28 percent in the previous week, while 36 percent underweighted it. The remaining 40 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 36 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 18 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $90.0 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM.
